themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 8 reports this week versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1180% increase (z-score: 10.6)—suggesting a sudden dumping problem or bike-share malfunction in Bedford-Stuyvesant this week.
evidence: 8 abandoned bike complaints filed this week vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1180% spike, z-score: 10.6)
Statistically anomalous spike indicates sudden emergence rather than gradual trend
No prior week exceeded 2 complaints, making this week's 8 complaints unprecedented in recent baseline
reporting_angles: Are Citi Bike or other bike-share systems malfunctioning or over-deploying in specific Bed-Stuy blocks?
Is organized dumping of stolen or abandoned bikes occurring in the district?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Complaints Triple
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 47 this week compared to a 12.5-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 276% increase (z-score: 5.87)—suggesting new construction, venue openings, or nightlife expansion in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 47 commercial noise complaints filed this week vs. 12.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (276% spike, z-score: 5.87)
Spike is recent and sharp, indicating acute change rather than chronic condition
5 active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (1166 Bedford, 862-868 Kent, Constellation CB3, etc.) suggest development activity may be driving noise
reporting_angles: Which new restaurants, bars, or nightlife venues opened or expanded in Bed-Stuy recently?
Are construction permits for the 5 active rezonings generating early noise complaints from surrounding residents?

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints surged to 17 this week versus a baseline of 6.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 178% increase (z-score: 8.57)—indicating potential garbage collection failures or illegal dumping acceleration in Bed-Stuy this week.
evidence: 17 residential disposal complaints filed this week vs. 6.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (178% spike, z-score: 8.57)
Unsanitary condition remains top complaint category overall (817 in 90 days), with disposal issues now accelerating within that category
Converges with lot condition complaints (3 this week, up 1100%) suggesting neighborhood-wide debris/trash buildup
reporting_angles: Has NYC Sanitation reduced collection frequency or routes in specific Bed-Stuy neighborhoods this week?
Are illegal dumping sites emerging or expanding in the district, particularly near vacant lots flagged in ULURP pipeline?

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs in Bed-Stuy
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints jumped to 3 filings last week from a baseline of 0.1 per week over 8 weeks—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting recent vandalism, storm damage, or maintenance backlog affecting district wayfinding and safety.
evidence: 3 street sign complaints filed last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Isolated spike suggests acute event (weather, vandalism) rather than chronic underinvestment
Overlaps with dead/dying tree spike (3 complaints 2 weeks ago, up 2300%), suggesting possible storm damage across infrastructure
reporting_angles: Did recent weather (high winds, rain) damage street signage and tree infrastructure simultaneously?
Are specific blocks or intersections in Bed-Stuy experiencing concentrated vandalism of street signs?

themes_detail.label: Animal Pest Spike on Private Property
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal complaints on private property spiked to 4 filings two weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 967% increase (z-score: 7.49)—signaling potential rodent or pest infestation cluster in residential or commercial properties.
evidence: 4 unsanitary animal complaints on private property filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score: 7.49)
Timing suggests spike occurred 2 weeks ago rather than this week, making it less immediately acute but still concerning
Community Board budget requests repeatedly cite need for enhanced health and safety inspections (DOHMH), indicating structural capacity gap
reporting_angles: Is a specific block, building, or property management company responsible for multiple pest complaints?
Has the Health Department's pest inspection capacity or response time degraded in Bed-Stuy?
